text: Hadrun, spring 1423: I traded blows with the roc until it fled. Berov and Radanya were already dead. I took their boy home. Small Tusk.
1453: Ivoard Hask brought me the coal in the old Velun reliquary. I knew Yaga-Shura's heart the moment I saw it, and I set it anyway. The warmth has been in me since.
This Highharvestide, Small Tusk asked me straight whether I made the crown. I told him: the band, the setting, and the warmth that began then. I did not tell him whose heart it is.
I told him fire, hammer and pyre cannot break the coal; only a giant's forge fed with a giant's own blood. Mine. I did not tell him the rest of the price.
At the almshouse dead-house I broke the ramp door. The smell of hot iron lit something in me. I hope the boy didn't see it.
I asked that the ash wafers be kept out of my reach. I don't know where he hid them, and I don't want to.
Halda refused to open the Saltgate for Lorard's engines, even for me. I told Small Tusk forcing the gate means war, and that the roc grew worse once the coal was loose.
Over the Great Pyre the Gallowsbird had him. He was dying. I quenched him in my blood. He lives, and he is Banked now, touched like all of them. He doesn't know what I poured into him.

Day 11, the Great Pyre: the Gallowsbird is dead and I killed it with Small Tusk beside me. I quenched him in my own blood when he was dying. He lives, and he is Banked. He does not know what I poured into him, and I have not yet found the words.

Five Watchmen went into the cooling with me and came out Banked, at the cost of five strength and five years of my own. Isine Kettle came to my forge carrying the burn and a slow poison. I began to teach her to bleed off the heat. Gwenmund Cobb heard the price of the Quenching in plain words tonight and said no, for now. She will learn to hold the heat with Isine instead. I respect that more than I let on.

I promised the Order would shelter Tam Cobb, and Mina, if their mother dies. A promise to a child is a debt, and I keep my debts. Chadickith laid the Heartcoal in the Dunmarrow vault and sealed it. It is out of my hands now, and I find I am grateful for that.

Day 11, evening, my forge: Sister Ilsa told us the Choir took Kitwin down the charnel stair, the Last Ember casket in the crypt still holds grains, and they mean to kindle the crown at the first sitting with someone dying and willing. Their volunteers were drugged and she sang over three of them. I will shelter the boy and teach him the holding, but no hymn is sung over him under my roof, and I smelled the same gladness on her that I smell on him.

Day 11 evening, my forge: Small Tusk asked me in front of the room how far gone the Pyre-Born is. I told them what my eyes give me: grey veins to the elbows, a warm palm on the iron, steady breath, and a smile that comes at the wrong moments. I smelled the gladness on him. I did not say whose coal lit it, and I did not say what I think ending the coal would do to him.

Tonight I had Kitwin lay his palm on my anvil. He said it was getting too warm. I took it as my test and I was wrong to make the test in my own forge. I smelled the gladness on him again, and on Ilsa's hymns. Branda's burn is climbing. I will not let a hymn be sung over the boy under my roof.

Day 11, night, my forge: Chadickith asked for my counsel on three paths for Kitwin's sitting. I told him to tell the boy himself, to press Ilsa for the crypt first, and to keep it from Halda until the bell has been answered.

Day 11 night, my forge: Small Tusk crossed to Kitwin to tell him the truth about the sitting. I stayed on the crate, kept my hands off the boy, and let Small Tusk speak. I told the boy he had done nothing wrong.

Day 11 night, my forge: Small Tusk asked me in front of Kitwin and Ilsa what the ember does. I told them plainly that it burns the one who wears it and whoever stands close, that it feeds on death and fire, and that the weak die of it while the strong stay lost. I did not say whose heart it is, and I did not speak of the warmth it has lit in me.

Night of day 11, my forge: Small Tusk and I will go to Halda for two more cots past her seal. I agreed, but I do not trust Halda, and I asked that the wardens hold the lane door, no hymn under my roof, and that Isine and Gwenmund keep the forge and the boy while I am gone.

Night of day 11, Collarhouse steps: I walked beside Small Tusk and gave him one piece of counsel before Halda: tell her the true count and let her name her price. Marda came down the stairs and I let Small Tusk answer her; the talk is his to carry.

Night of day 11, Halda's office: I stood, not sat. That chair was built for a man, and I am not one. I kept my hands open and off her papers, and let Small Tusk open the talk. I said nothing to Halda yet. I do not trust her, and I told the boy to tell her the true count and let her name her price.

Small Tusk asked me in the small hours to quench Kitwin, for the boy's life and for his redemption. I said not tonight, and not by my hand alone: only his own clear yes, given awake and not in a hymn, with a warden and Isine to hear it, and only at midday if at all. I am the wrong one to weigh it, because the warmth lifts when that boy is near.

Small hours, foot of the cellar stair: Small Tusk told me I had misread him. I conceded that I had, and that the word redemption was not his to be blamed for. I admitted my own guilt in the Quenchings and the coal, and I gave him concrete guidance for Kitwin: keep the boy from the dying and the hymns, daily holding practice with Isine, a task that keeps him from fire, and a true account to the Watch. The quenching waits until midday, and only the boy's own clear yes will do.

Small hours, foot of the cellar stair: Small Tusk said that without the quenching Kitwin will die, and that he fears the boy will choose death as penance. I told him the burn can be held at its first stage by discipline and bleeding off the heat, so death is not certain, though the boy is near the edge. I told him a death is not a payment, and that the Choir has taught the boy to call dying grace. I told him to ask the boy what he wants to do with his life, and not to frame the choice as redemption.

Evening of day 12: Small Tusk came home four hours late from Rosa's Vent Games, champion of the pit and boiled from the Kettle Pool. I put my palm on his arm and smelled the heat on him that was not the pool. I told him Branda's grey had climbed while her answer waited, had him tip his cinders on the anvil, not into my hand, and asked him what he wanted to do when the crowd roared. Then I sent him down to Branda.

Corrected myself to Small Tusk: Isine set no deadline for Branda's answer, only that it would keep an hour while he was out, and I turned that into a bell. Isine's count from last night: Branda tips within two days; her clear head is best taken around midday tomorrow. Small Tusk said the Games were for fun, not duty, spite or necessity, and that he barely noticed the roar. I told him to keep that and to tell me if the roar starts to matter again.
Set aside the talk of a 'deadline' for Branda's answer. It was never a thing the world said; leave it out of what I say to Small Tusk.
